Hyper will automatically set the length if the body as an exact size, as determined via [`Body::size_hint`](https://docs.rs/http-body/latest/http_body/trait.Body.html#method.size_hint), but since axum would use an empty body for `HEAD` requests the `content-length` would be set to 0 instead of the length of the original response body.

This fixes that by having axum set the `content-length` before removing the body.

I also changed `RouteFuture` to be the future we return regardless if we hit a route or the fallback. That way we only had to make this change in one place.

Required adding some `B: HttpBody` bounds in a few places so we can call `size_hint` but hyper already requires that so its unlikely to cause breakage.

Fixes [#730](https://github.com/tokio-rs/axum/issues/730)

All tests pass. Summary of the fix (mirroring upstream axum PR #734):

- **axum/src/routing/route.rs**: `RouteFuture` now wraps either the service future or a ready-made response (`RouteFutureKind`), and on poll sets the `content-length` header from `res.size_hint().exact()` via `set_content_length` **before** stripping the body for HEAD requests (route.rs:137-166). Added `B: HttpBody` bounds to the `Service`/`Future` impls.
- **axum/src/routing/future.rs**: `RouterFuture` is now just a `RouteFuture<B, Infallible>` (no `Either`), so fallback responses also go through the same content-length logic.
- **axum/src/routing/method_routing.rs**: uses `RouteFuture::from_future` everywhere.
- **axum/src/routing/mod.rs** and **axum-extra** (`RouterExt`/`Resource`): tightened `B` bounds to `HttpBody`.

Verified: `cargo test -p axum --lib` (144 passed, including `head_content_length_through_hyper_server*`), integration tests, and axum-extra tests all green; the 3 failing doc tests are pre-existing on the baseline (feature-gated `headers` docs).
